name: Serer (Seereer)
notes: Serer (Seereer-Siin), Northern Atlantic (Senegambian) branch of Atlantic-Congo, spoken mainly in the Sine-Saloum region of Senegal. The 2005-standardized Latin orthography is close to phonemic: ⟨c⟩ = palatal stop /c/, ⟨j⟩ = /ɟ/ (as in the closely related Wolof), ⟨ñ⟩ = /ɲ/, ⟨ŋ⟩ = /ŋ/, ⟨y⟩ = /j/. Five oral vowel qualities /i e a o u/ contrast length, written by doubling the vowel letter (a/aa, e/ee, i/ii, o/oo, u/uu), mirroring the vowel-length pattern of the related Fula (ff) and Wolof (wo) specs. Serer has a rare series of VOICELESS implosives (Ᵽ/ƥ /ɓ̥/, Ƭ/ƭ /ɗ̥/) alongside the more cross-linguistically common voiced implosives (Ɓ/ɓ /ɓ/, Ɗ/ɗ /ɗ/, Ƈ/ƈ /ʄ/) — a Niger-Congo substrate feature shared with other Senegambian languages. Word-initial prenasalized stops are written ⟨mb nd nj ng nq⟩; the uvular prenasalized ⟨nq⟩ is analysed here as [ɴq] by analogy with the other nasal+stop digraphs, pending direct phonetic confirmation. This spec is quality:research — grapheme values are drawn from the cited Wikipedia orthography table and cross-checked against the general Senegambian pattern shared by ff.json and wo.json, not against a full primary phonological description letter-by-letter.
